subject: SummitCare HIPAA capabilities questionnaire — clarifications and BAA exhibit
messages:
From: Kerry O'Neill <kerry.oneill@summitcare.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Martin Liu <martin.liu@summitcare.com>, Angela Park <angela.park@healthprocure.io>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SummitCare HIPAA questionnaire: a few clarifications

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for sending the questionnaire earlier today. We have a short procurement window and a couple of technical/legal clarifications before we can move the draft through security and legal at SummitCare. Can you confirm the following?

1) Data residency: For hosted customers, can we restrict region to US-East only and ensure no replication outside the region?
2) PHI in transit: Do you enforce mandatory TLS1.2+ for all API and control-plane traffic? Any exceptions for legacy integrations?
3) Encryption keys: Is BYOK supported for private deployments and for Dedicated customers? If so, which KMS providers are validated?
4) Subprocessors: We need an up-to-date list of subprocessors (including cloud infra, monitoring, and logging vendors) and whether any subprocessors see unredacted PHI.
5) Logging & retention: What logs are retained by default (request/response, metadata only) and what are the options to shorten retention to 90 days?

Also, can you share your most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a draft of your BAA exhibit? Legal will want to review before we hand it to procurement.

We attached an updated copy of our questionnaire with specific line-items highlighted — please respond inline where possible. Looking to close this in the next 10 business days.

Thanks,
Kerry O'Neill
Director, Information Security
SummitCare Systems
Attachments: SummitCare_HIPAA_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet with highlighted questions)
From: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kerry O'Neill <kerry.oneill@summitcare.com>
Cc: Martin Liu <martin.liu@summitcare.com>, Angela Park <angela.park@healthprocure.io>, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SummitCare HIPAA questionnaire: a few clarifications

Kerry — thanks for the clear list. I've looped in Priyom (Security) and Vivek (Solutions) for technical details; Monica (Legal Ops) will own the BAA draft. High level answers below and I attached a concise capability matrix that maps to the rows in your questionnaire.

Quick answers (high level):
- Region: Hosted customers can be pinned to a US-East-only tenancy; we do not replicate PHI outside the pinned region by default. We will include a region-constraint clause in the BAA exhibit.
- Transport: All customer-facing APIs and control plane traffic are encrypted with TLS1.2+ and we mandate TLS1.3 where supported. No planned exceptions for PHI traffic.
- Keys: BYOK is supported on Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments; for Hosted customers we offer KMS-integrated envelope encryption (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault for Dedicated/Private).
- Subprocessors: Attached matrix includes a current subprocessors list. No subprocessors have access to unredacted PHI in normal operations; monitoring/log aggregation receives metadata and redacted request traces.
- Logging & retention: Default telemetry (request metadata + request ids) retained 365 days; payloads are not retained unless a customer enables long-term logging. Shorter retention windows (90 days) are configurable on Dedicated/Private and as an add-on for Hosted.

Attachments sent: Redwood_HIPAA_Capability_Matrix_2026-04-12.csv, Redwood_BAA_draft_v1.1.pdf, redwood_network_dataflow.png

Proposed next steps:
1) Priyom to answer line-items 12-27 in the spreadsheet inline by EOD tomorrow.
2) Monica to upload a redlineable BAA (see attached) and request any contract addenda.
3) Schedule a technical 30-min call (we have availability Tue/Wed morning PT) to run through deployment/residency architecture.

If that works I'll send a DocuSign link for the BAA exhibit and a calendar invite for a technical call.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive — Healthcare
Redwood Inference

Aditya / team — thanks for the fast response and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups after reviewing the capability matrix:

- For hosted customers, when you say "pinned to US-East tenancy," does that mean logical tenant isolation or a dedicated cloud account/project per customer? We need assurance that data residency is enforceable and auditable.
- Regarding monitoring traces: can we provide a sample (redacted) trace showing what you classify as "metadata" vs "payload"? That will help our IR/security reviewers.
- BAA: our legal team highlighted two clauses for redline: 1) subprocessor notification timeline (we require 30 days prior notice), and 2) breach notification SLA (we require 72 hours max). Your current draft has 60 days and 5 business days respectively.

Procurement timeline: if we can get inline answers to rows 12-27 and an updated BAA redline by Fri Apr 16, we can aim to get to final sign-off by Apr 23.

Thanks — Martin
Martin Liu
Sr. Procurement Manager, SummitCare Systems

On Mon, Apr 13, 2026 at 2:05 PM Martin Liu <martin.liu@summitcare.com> wrote:
> Aditya / team — thanks for the fast response and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups after reviewing the capability matrix:
>
> - For hosted customers, when you say "pinned to US-East tenancy," does that mean logical tenant isolation or a dedicated cloud account/project per customer?

Hi all — quick technical clarifications inline below and in the attached updated capability matrix (we added row-level notes):

1) Isolation: For Hosted customers we provide logical tenant isolation within a compliant US-East deployment. For customers requiring physical separation, we offer Dedicated (reserved capacity) with a dedicated cloud account/project and isolated VPC. We will add a contract clause that defines these options and the associated controls for audit.

2) Monitoring traces: We can produce a sanitized example trace. "Metadata" includes request timestamps, route, response time, token counts, and hashed request id; "payload" refers to the request/response text. By default payloads are not stored for PHI unless a customer enables retention for debugging. Example: attached redwood_network_dataflow.png and a sanitized trace snippet in the CSV.

3) Subprocessors: Current subprocessors (infra and managed services) are listed in the matrix. We will agree to a 30 day notification window for subprocessor additions for SummitCare and we can include a right-to-review clause for new subprocessors.

4) Breach notification: Redwood's standard SLA is 5 business days; we are willing to commit to a 72-hour notification window for incidents involving confirmed unauthorized access to PHI. Monica will circulate an updated BAA redline that reflects both changes.

Action items assigned:
- Priyom: update questionnaire rows 12-27 with inline technical notes (ETA EOD Tue).
- Vivek: prepare a 30-min architecture demo and plan for Tue/Wed morning PT; include a short runbook for on-call incident handling.
- Monica: circulate BAA redline with the 30-day subprocessor notification and 72-hour breach notification.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Sr. Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
